item.title: 'Biggest oil deal in history': Trump announces US control of 65bn barrels in Venezuela
item.description: Trump said the deal was negotiated by Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth and Venezuela's interim President Delcy Rodriguez. He announced the agreement in a social media post. The announcement comes almost nine months after the US military, acting on Trump's orders, carried out an operation to capture Venezuela's President Nicolás Maduro. Maduro was taken to the US to face federal charges related to narcoterrorism, drug trafficking.
item.dc:creator: RAJEEV SINGH

item.title: Delhi model murder: Accused Imran was booked for sexually harassing minor in 2018
item.description: A gym trainer accused of murdering a young woman was injured in a police encounter. He opened fire at officers while resisting arrest in Rajouri Garden. Police retaliated, and three bullets struck the suspect in his legs. Investigators are probing his social media activity and past criminal cases. The suspect had allegedly harassed the victim before her death.
item.dc:creator: ABHAY

item.title: CNG price hike: Compressed natural gas gets costlier; check city-wise rates
item.description: Consumers in Delhi and surrounding areas brace for higher compressed natural gas prices as Indraprastha Gas Limited implements a price hike due to escalating imported liquefied natural gas costs. Effective August 29, this change is linked to surging international LNG prices and ongoing Middle East conflicts, impacting both freight and passenger fares in the region, following several prior increases.
item.dc:creator: SHIVANGHI PAYAL

item.title: ‘India messed up big time’: Ex-captain sounds alarm after costly Colombo blunder
item.description: India's ambitions for World Test Championship qualification took a blow following a drawn Test match in Colombo. This result denied them a chance to sweep the series against Sri Lanka. Cricketer Krishnamachari Srikkanth expressed concerns about the implications for the team's future. With only seven matches left, India must secure victories in at least six to stay in contention for the title.
item.dc:creator: PRANAV SHUKLA

item.title: Pak drone detected in J&K's Rajouri, security forces put LoC sector on high alert
item.description: Security forces are on high alert after a Pakistani drone was detected near the LoC. Military personnel tracked the unmanned aerial vehicle over the Rajouri sector on Friday evening. This incident follows several other suspected drone sightings reported in Jammu and Kashmir recently. Security forces have intensified search operations in forward areas to detect any dropped materials. Border monitoring remains active as authorities await further official updates on the situation.
item.dc:creator: YASHASVI VASISTHA

item.title: Zohran Mamdani forms business council as JPMorgan, BlackRock, Google & others push back
item.description: Mayor Zohran Mamdani has established a new Business Advisory Council. This group includes fifteen prominent business leaders from various sectors. Some major corporate executives declined to join the new council. The council will meet quarterly to offer strategic guidance to the mayor. This initiative aims to foster collaboration between city hall and business leaders.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: PCB’s Lord’s Test threat exposed? Sarfaraz Ahmed breaks silence amid controversy
item.description: Pakistan's head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed stated players were unaware of a reported PCB threat. This controversy emerged during the lunch break on the first day. The interview featured Imran Khan's sons discussing their father's situation. Pakistan's players returned to the field after lunch and the Test continued. England ended the second day in a strong position.
item.dc:creator: PRANAV SHUKLA

item.title: Nepal floods: Missing tally rises to 2,482, including 320 Indians; disaster toll hits 584
item.description: Hundreds died and thousands are missing after a disaster in Nepal and Tibet. Rescue operations faced repeated setbacks due to overflowing barrier lakes and new avalanches. Indian nationals in Nepal remain uncontactable, with authorities seeking clarity from Nepalese officials. Several Indian nationals have been safely rescued from affected areas in Nepal. The situation remains dynamic as authorities work to reconcile missing persons reports.
item.dc:creator: VISHANT AGARWALA

item.title: Sonia Gandhi's memoir row deepens, Congress alleges government pressure
item.description: Penguin Random House India has made the decision not to publish Sonia Gandhi's memoir, leading to allegations from Congress regarding external pressure to omit references to Modi and China. In response, Penguin emphasized its commitment to editorial integrity and its role in verifying facts. They remain open to publishing the memoir in India, but uncertainties linger surrounding the rights for its release in the country.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: Teens on Instagram & Facebook get 11 new protections under Meta deal
item.description: Meta agreed to an eighteen billion dollar settlement with fifty-two attorneys general. The company will implement major protective overhauls for under-eighteen users across its platforms. These changes include time limits and automatic night mode for minors. Automatic screen-time alerts and hidden like counts will also be introduced. Enhanced age assurance systems and content guardrails will protect younger users.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: Why Aug 29 Matters? National Sports Day honours Dhyan Chand; story of the Wizard
item.description: On August 29, National Sports Day commemorates Major Dhyan Chand, the iconic figure in Indian hockey whose brilliance led to three Olympic gold medals. This day not only celebrates his legacy, but also promotes the spirit of sportsmanship, fitness, and healthy living among the youth, as well as acknowledging the accolades of India's sports heroes, fueling inspiration for future generations.
item.dc:creator: HIJAM RAJU SINGH

item.title: £3M Bath mansion faces demolition calls from 100+ residents
item.description: A millionaire’s £3 million mega-mansion in Bath has sparked a planning dispute, with more than 100 residents calling for the seven-bedroom property to be torn down. Locals claim the home is significantly taller and larger than plans approved by Bath and North East Somerset Council. The developer denies deliberately bypassing planning rules.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: $70K underground Missouri home from 1976 survived F4 tornado, still hidden
item.description: Built in 1976 for $70,000, a remarkable underground home in Springfield, Missouri, was designed to blend into the hillside while providing strength and energy efficiency. Nearly 50 years later, the concrete residence remains largely hidden from view and has an extraordinary history, including surviving a devastating F4 tornado that struck the neighbourhood in 1990.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: AI tests 40 of 100 million ways to 3D-print a NASA rocket alloy & found 6 that worked
item.description: Washington State University researchers used artificial intelligence to find better printing methods. This advance significantly reduces the cost and time for printing a critical metal alloy. The AI strategy successfully identified printable configurations for the GRCop-42 alloy. This innovation makes the alloy accessible for use on common commercial 3D printers. The AI approach could also accelerate discoveries in other scientific fields.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: WC: Belgium break Indian hearts in shootout as Harmanpreet’s side finishes eighth
item.description: India's spirited hockey fightback concluded with heartbreak against Belgium. The teams played to a thrilling 3-3 draw in regulation time. Belgium ultimately prevailed in a tense penalty shootout after the match. India had initially taken the lead through Abhishek's early field goal. Harmanpreet Singh scored twice to force the shootout, but Belgium won.
item.dc:creator: TOI SPORTS DESK

item.title: Toxic Day 3: Yash starrer dips 29.3%, earns Rs 23.75 cr overseas
item.description: Yash and Nayanthara's film 'Toxic' continues its theatrical run after a strong opening. The movie recorded a drop in its domestic earnings on its third day. However, it managed to cross the Rs 150 crore net mark in India. Its worldwide gross collection now stands at Rs 221.45 crore after three days. The Geetu Mohandas directorial has garnered significant attention from audiences.
item.dc:creator: TOI ENTERTAINMENT DESK

item.title: Travis Kelce turns childhood nostalgia into $200 million business move
item.description: Travis Kelce is expanding his business portfolio with a major investment alongside JANA Partners, taking a 9% stake in an amusement park company. The move has a personal connection for the Kansas City Chiefs star, who grew up in Ohio near Cedar Point and has long loved theme parks. The investment comes as the company faces financial challenges, while Kelce continues building interests beyond football, including Formula 1 and brand partnerships.
item.dc:creator: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK

item.title: Stephen and Ayesha Curry’s foundation helps over 7,500 Oakland students
item.description: Stephen Curry and his wife, ayesha Curry, have marked a major milestone in bridging the literacy gap in their hometown through their foundation.
item.dc:creator: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK

item.title: Travis Kelce takes 5% ownership stake in product he has used for years
item.description: In January 2026, Travis Kelce expanded his growing business portfolio by taking a 5% ownership stake in a company whose product he has relied on for years. The NFL star said it had remained “a constant through different seasons” of his career and life. The investment reflects Kelce’s focus on recovery while strengthening his presence beyond football through strategic partnerships and ownership opportunities.
item.dc:creator: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK

item.title: Jio Platforms gets Sebi nod for 37.7k cr IPO, set to be India's biggest
item.description: Jio Platforms received Sebi clearance for its initial public offering. The company aims to raise up to four billion dollars in this debut. This offering is expected to become India's largest stock market listing. Jio plans a pure primary issue, with proceeds retiring debt. Reliance Industries holds a majority stake in Jio Platforms.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: Junk foods will soon have labels warning of high salt, sugar and fat
item.description: Junk foods will soon feature prominent red warning labels on their packaging. These labels will highlight high levels of salt, sugar, and fat content. The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India has agreed to this new regulation. This move aims to help consumers make more informed purchasing decisions. The phased implementation will allow the industry time to adjust product formulations.
item.dc:creator: ANUJA JAISWAL

item.title: Nepal floods: Spooked by visuals, tourists cancel bookings, tour operators hit
item.description: A Darjeeling couple had planned a 15-day trip to Mansarovar via Kerung in Sept. The Rs 4.4-lakh tour package included permits for entering Tibet. They cancelled the trip after watching videos of Kerung being swept away. Kolkata travel agents Anil Punjabi and Anjani Dhanuka had furrowed brows over rising cancellations even as many sought updates on the safety of other Nepal destinations like Kathmandu, Pokhara, Patan and Lumbini.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: From Reds to NGOs: RSS weekly expands ‘dimagi Naxal’ label
item.description: In an editorial, ‘Organiser’ termed NAC as marking the “classic takeover of the ‘dimagi Naxals’ of governance”. It said, “As the armed rebellion has failed miserably, the dimagi variant has taken charge.” The editorial added penetrating bureaucracy, policy machinery, legal system, academia, media and NGOs formed part of this “revolutionary strategy”.
item.dc:creator: MANASH PRATIM GOHAIN

item.title: National Testing Agency gets three senior officers amid exam overhaul
item.description: IPS officer Ravi Kumar Singh and IAS officer Prasanna Venkatesh V have been appointed directors at NTA, while Amit Samdariya, a 2016-batch Indian Revenue Service (customs and indirect taxes) officer, will join as joint director. The appointments were cleared through separate personnel ministry orders dated August 27. The personnel ministry has directed all three officers to take charge within three weeks.
item.dc:creator: MANASH PRATIM GOHAIN

item.title: India has 7,500 Himalayan glacial lakes, 200 are high risk amid flood fears
item.description: Nepal's alarming glacial lake outburst flood serves as a wake-up call for India, which is home to about 200 vulnerable glacial lakes in the Himalayas. The GLOF incident in Sikkim resulted in severe damage, highlighting the urgency of proactive measures. In response, the Indian government has launched a National GLOF Risk Mitigation Programme focused on thorough assessments, continuous monitoring, effective early warnings, and raising awareness within local communities.
item.dc:creator: PRADEEP THAKUR

item.title: Clean energy push unfair on developing nations: CJI Surya Kant
item.description: Speaking at the Commonwealth Secretariat in London, CJI Kant said, “Countries that are finally industrialising are being asked to move rapidly towards renewable power, and are often made to bear the brunt of criticism when they cannot move fast enough.” “The challenge, therefore, is to reconcile the urgency of the clean energy transition with the principles of fairness and shared responsibility that must underpin it,” the CJI said.
item.dc:creator: DHANANJAY MAHAPATRA

item.title: Nilekani committee seeks public ideas to fix exams
item.description: The panel, headed by Infosys co-founder and technology expert Nandan Nilekani, was announced by Prime Minister Narendra Modi last month amid heightened scrutiny of the examination system following NEET-UG paper leak controversy and youth protests over alleged lapses in the test’s conduct. It will also look at measures to improve accessibility and inclusion, while factoring in student well-being during the examination process.
item.dc:creator: BHARTI JAIN AND MANASH PRATIM GOHAIN

item.title: Power reversal: Nepal may import from India
item.description: Due to severe flooding that has hampered power generation in Nepal, India may begin exporting electricity to its neighboring country. The flash floods on Wednesday severely affected Nepal's hydropower and solar output. This unexpected turn of events could alter the traditional power exchange, as India's current electricity generation exceeds domestic demand. They are connected by a 1,000MW transmission line for energy trade.
item.dc:creator: ATUL MATHUR

item.title: India's Javelin buy: What 60 battle-tested US missiles add to Army’s arsenal
item.description: India is set to enhance its defense capabilities by acquiring the Javelin anti-tank missile system from the United States. This strategic deal signifies a potential boost in co-production avenues for both countries’ industries. The Indian Army has entered into a Letter of Offer and Acceptance, marking a vital step in strengthening India-US defense ties. The Javelin, known for its man-portable design, is essential for neutralizing armored targets.
item.dc:creator: ARYAN SINGH

item.title: Why India and China are betting on the Northern Sea Route & why it matters
item.description: India’s interest in the Northern Sea Route is being shaped by two factors: its commercial potential and the need to broaden trade connectivity. The NSR also offers a clear geographical advantage on certain Asia-Europe trade lanes.
item.dc:creator: SMRITI JAIN

item.title: ‘Go and educate yourself’: Anaya hits back at Marizanne Kapp over cricket return
item.description: Anaya Bangar urged critics to educate themselves on transgender inclusion in sports. She is seeking a pathway back into competitive women's cricket after surgery. Cricket Australia has cleared her for elite play under specific policy requirements. Bangar aims to prove herself at the community level before aiming for the Women's Big Bash League. Her eligibility for elite cricket is subject to ongoing policy compliance and performance.
item.dc:creator: TOI SPORTS DESK

item.title: 3,400 SIR forms found at Navi Mumbai photocopy shop; 5 BLOs suspended
item.description: A significant controversy arose when five Booth Level Officers were suspended after voter enumeration forms were found in a photocopy shop. This event ignited tensions between Shiv Sena (UBT) and BJP activists in Navi Mumbai. Authorities seized numerous printed Special Intensive Revision forms from the premises, and a case was filed against an individual for illegal possession. The opposition has since questioned the validity of the voter roll revision efforts.
item.dc:creator: PRACHI KUMAWAT

item.title: ‘Locals cautioned, driver reversed’: How warning saved Andhra pilgrims from Nepal floods
item.description: A group of pilgrims from Andhra Pradesh narrowly escaped devastating flash floods in Nepal. A brief tea break and a local warning allowed their bus driver to reverse to safety. Another bus traveling with them was caught in the disaster and hit a bridge. The incident occurred on August 25th while they were traveling towards the China border. This experience highlights how small delays can avert tragedy during natural disasters.
item.dc:creator: PRACHI KUMAWAT

item.title: Hockey India rewards women’s team with Rs 50 lakh after historic World Cup finish
item.description: In a remarkable achievement, Hockey India has granted fifty lakh rupees to the women's team following their impressive fifth-place finish in the World Cup, their best in fifty-two years. The team successfully defeated Germany in their concluding match and only faced one defeat during the tournament. This honor not only rewards their dedication but also motivates them for future challenges.
item.dc:creator: TOI SPORTS DESK

item.title: SBI PO prelims result 2026 released: Direct link to download scorecard
item.description: The State Bank of India (SBI) has declared the Probationary Officer (PO) Prelims Result 2026 for candidates who appeared in the August 1 and 2 examination. The result is available on the official SBI Careers portal. Candidates shortlisted through the preliminary stage can now proceed to the Mains examination for recruitment against 1,500 PO vacancies.
item.dc:creator: TOI Education

item.title: 'Frustrated' with childcare, Faridabad woman slits 2-year-old’s neck; arrested
item.description: A disturbing case emerged from Faridabad where a mother is accused of assaulting her toddler son with a paper cutter, causing serious injuries to his neck. The child was treated promptly and is recovering. The situation escalated when the father reported the incident to the police. Investigators discovered that the mother was facing intense strain from her childcare duties, leading to her arrest on an attempted murder charge.
item.dc:creator: NIKHIL SHARMA
